content:
incident-bot: ⚠️ High alert volume detected: inference-gateway 5xx-rate > 18% (15m) in us-west-2. PagerDuty triggers: 7. Runbook: <https://redwood.runbooks/inference/pgd-flood>
Maria (oncall): I'm picking this up. Notifying PD and starting triage. Any customer-facing errors reported?
Kevin: No customer tickets yet. Backend retries have spiked; looks like an intermittent downstream auth failure. Traces show many short-lived 502s from gpu-proxy.
Jon: Noted. The alert stream is also noisy — many duplicate alerts for the same trace_id. We're getting page storms.
Maria (oncall): Prioritize: 1) stop the page storm 2) confirm customer impact 3) apply mitigation. I'll do a temporary squelch on lower-sev alerts.
Maria (oncall): /pd acknowledge 1978887777
sre-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Maria. Incident key: PD-32412. Current escalation policy: inference-sre
Lisa: For immediate noise control: can we apply an alert-router rule to coalesce by trace_id and drop duplicates for 5m?
Kevin: Yes. We have an experimental alert-router. I'll flip the rule now: route.alert_group_by = trace_id, dedupe_window=300s.
Kevin: Pushing rule:
```
# alert-router patch
- match: inference-gateway
  group_by: [trace_id]
  dedupe_seconds: 300
```
Kevin: applied — should reduce duplicate pages within 5m.
Maria (oncall): Good. Also temporarily increase the minimum severity to page: severity >= error (silence info/warn). Applying silence on Prometheus alerts labeled severity=info for 30m.
Maria (oncall): /alertmanager silence add --matcher="severity=info" --duration=30m
sre-bot: Alertmanager: Silence created id=sl-9a8b duration=30m
Jon: We should also rate-limit Slack notifications. Right now one alert -> multiple channel posts. Propose token-bucket limiter (burst 3, refill 1/10s) at slack-proxy.
Ashish: Implemented token-bucket on slack-proxy. Config:
```
slack_proxy:
  rate_limit:
    mode: token_bucket
    burst: 3
    refill_per_sec: 0.1
```
Ashish: Pushed. Expect lower channel spam in ~30s.
Lisa: While those are in flight, I'm opening a quick dashboard to track unique incidents vs duplicate counts so we can verify mitigation.
Lisa: Dashboard URL: <https://grafana.internal/d/alerts/unique-alerts?orgId=1&var-service=inference-gateway>
Maria (oncall): Customer impact update: no user-facing errors in our frontend metrics, but internal retries could increase latency for heavy workloads. I'll note impact as: "degraded backend success rate, no customer-visible outage".
Jon: For PD routing: move any repeated PD triggers for the same trace_id into a single PD incident to avoid multiple pages. Suggest matching on trace_id in PD integration.
Kevin: We can change the PD webhook dedupe logic, but that's a risky change during incident. Instead: add a PD throttle rule: max 1 incident per trace_id per 10m.
Maria (oncall): Approving PD throttle for 10m. Kevin, please apply and comment here when done.
Kevin: Applied PD throttle: rule id pd-throttle-1978, window=10m, key=trace_id
Kevin: /pd config show pd-throttle-1978
```
name: pd-throttle-1978
scope: inference-gateway
key: trace_id
window_sec: 600
max_incidents: 1
```
Kevin: Confirmed active.
Maria (oncall): Great. Next: we need a short post-incident task list. I'll create a ticket and assign owners.
Maria (oncall): Creating ticket: PROJ-1123 "Adjust alerting defaults for inference-gateway: grouping, PD throttle, slack rate limiting"
Maria (oncall): Assigned: Kevin (alert-router + PD throttle followup), Lisa (dashboards + eval), Jon (runbook update), Ashish (slack-proxy rate-limit permanence)
Ashish: I'll also add a small metrics tag to alerts: "dedupe_key=trace_id" so we can measure unique incident reduction.
Lisa: On follow-up, propose increasing dedupe_window to 600s for this service and add a regression test so we don't accidentally merge noisy alerts later.
Jon: Agreed. Also add a synthetic that simulates repeated failures and asserts aggregated alerts = 1.
Maria (oncall): Handoff: I'm on call for 12 more minutes, then Jon takes over. Jon — I'll drop a summary in PD and update the runbook with these temp mitigations.
Maria (oncall): Summary -> PD: "Applied alert-router grouping by trace_id (300s), PD throttle (1 incident per trace_id per 10m), silence severity=info for 30m, slack-proxy token-bucket limiter(3 burst,0.1 rps). No customer-facing errors reported. Owner assignments created."
sre-bot: PD: Incident PD-32412 updated. Comments added.
Jon: I'll watch the dashboard for the next 30m and follow up on ticket PROJ-1123 after handoff.
Maria (oncall): Thanks team. If noise creeps back, escalate to L2 and we'll consider temporarily routing to a rotation channel not tied to PD.
Kevin: Logs of the root cause: downstream auth service returning intermittent 502 under load. I'll open a bug and link to this incident.
Kevin: Bug created: INF-781 - "auth-service: transient 502s under burst; investigate circuit breaker"
Maria (oncall): Marking this thread as incident mitigation coordination. We'll do a full postmortem if customer impact rises or if mitigations don't hold.
Jon: Noted. Handoff to me in 2 min.
Maria (oncall): handing off now — Jon you have the incident.
Jon: Taking over. Monitoring dashboard; will update PD if anything changes. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Incident PD-32412 reassigned to Jon. Acknowledged.
Maria (oncall): ending handoff. Follow-up ticket PROJ-1123 includes steps and owners. Closing slack noise for now. :white_check_mark:
